Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: MODULE 3. OBJECTS & PERSONAL SPACE
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: 3.1 Everyday Objects
- Materials: vocabulary cards, audio, reading handout
Warm-up: say one word you already know for this topic.
Recycles have got and classroom vocabulary.
Recycled language: phone, computer, book.
Answer from memory: which word belongs to this topic?
Which word belongs to this topic?
Core Active Vocabulary (13 items):

phone — a telephone. Example: My phone is in my bag.
computer — a machine for storing and using data. Example: The computer is on the desk.
book — pages with text you read. Example: This book is interesting.
bag — a container you carry things in. Example: My wallet is in the bag.
key — a small metal object that opens a lock. Example: This is my house key.
wallet — a small case for money and cards. Example: I have got a brown wallet.
pen — a tool for writing with ink. Example: Can I borrow your pen?
paper — thin material for writing on. Example: There is paper on the desk.
notebook — a small book for writing notes. Example: I have got a notebook.
cup — a small container for hot drinks. Example: The cup is empty.
plate — a flat dish for food. Example: The plate is on the table.
glass — a container for cold drinks, or the material. Example: A glass of water, please.
knife — a tool for cutting. Example: The knife is on the plate.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• What is this?
• It is a ...
• Can I have a ...?
• Where is the ...?
• It is on the table.

Grammar focus: Articles (a / an / the).
Use a before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound: a book, an apple. Use the for a specific object: the book on the table.
